item: the re-index resume drain and the article-index build stand aside while the storage guard is engaged
summary: The guard paused collection, the housekeeping lane and the heavy reads while a reader pinned the write-ahead log, but the re-index resume drain and the article-index build never asked, so the log reached 80 and 220 GB in the field. StorageGuard.wait_if_engaged gained should_stop and on_wait, and engaged_now answers once without waiting; the drain waits at the top of its batch loop (no session, no corpus lease) and a running call is asked to return at a window boundary after the first (a commit has ended the transaction by then), then the same batch is run again from its cursor; the index build waits before each statement with the attempt record given back for the length of the wait, and takes nothing once the app is quitting in order. Both follow the log and the drive latch, say why on the job row (keyed x12), resume by themselves and still end on a stop. Every mutant of the new checks is killed by the new tests, on a harness that refuses a verdict without a passing baseline.
